app.title: DOAJ Pre-Assessment Tool
app.subtitle: Self-test your journal against DOAJ application criteria before you apply.
app.disclaimer: Note: This tool uses AI to analyse URLs you provide. Results are indicative only and may contain errors — always verify independently before applying to DOAJ.
step.openAccess.title: 1. Open Access Compliance
step.openAccess.adheresToDefinition: The journal adheres to the DOAJ definition of open access.
step.openAccess.hasNoEmbargo: Articles are immediately open access upon publication (no embargo period).
step.openAccess.statementHint: Public page declaring the journal's open access policy.
step.about.title: 2. About the Journal
step.copyright.title: 3. Copyright & Licensing
step.copyright.embedsLicense: Each article embeds machine-readable license metadata.
step.copyright.consistencyHint: DOAJ checks three locations: the general policy page, individual article pages, and article PDFs. All three must show the same license and copyright terms. Inconsistencies are a common rejection reason.
step.copyright.licenseConsistentOnArticl: License on individual article pages matches the site-wide license policy.
step.copyright.licenseConsistentInPdfs: License text in article PDFs matches the website license policy.
step.copyright.noCopyrightConflicts: No copyright conflicts across the website, article pages, and PDFs (e.g. no 'All rights reserved' next to an open license).
step.editorial.title: 4. Editorial Process
step.editorial.avgWeeks: Average weeks from submission to publication
step.editorial.endogenyCompliant: In-house authorship does not exceed 25% (editors/board members are not authors of more than 25% of published articles).
step.editorial.endogenyHint: DOAJ rule: count the last two issues (or last calendar year if continuous publishing). If any author of a research article is also an editor, board member, or reviewer, that article counts as in-house. Maximum 25%.
step.editorial.articleDatesDisplayed: Article pages display submission, acceptance, and/or publication dates.
step.editorial.articleDatesHint: DOAJ strongly recommends showing at least two of these three dates on each article page. This is a transparency signal checked during evaluation.
step.businessModel.title: 6. Business Model
step.businessModel.chargesApc: The journal charges article processing charges (APCs).
step.businessModel.providesWaiver: The journal provides waivers for authors who cannot pay.
step.businessModel.chargesOtherFees: The journal charges other fees (submission, publication, etc.).
step.businessModel.otherFeesInfoHint: Public page listing all other author-facing fees (submission fees, page charges, colour printing, etc.) and when they apply.
step.ethics.title: 5. Ethics & Research Integrity
step.ethics.description: DOAJ requires journals to have clear policies for research integrity. Missing or vague ethics policies are a frequent rejection reason.
step.ethics.publicationEthicsHint: Page describing how the journal handles plagiarism, data fabrication, duplicate publication, and conflicts of interest.
step.ethics.hasRetractionsPolicy: The journal has a publicly stated policy for corrections, retractions, and expressions of concern.
step.ethics.retractionHint: The policy must describe how the journal handles post-publication issues and how notices will be labelled.
step.ethics.hasConflictPolicy: The journal has a policy on conflicts of interest and authorship criteria for authors, reviewers, and editors.
step.ethics.indexingClaimsVerifiable: All indexing and ranking claims on the journal website are accurate and verifiable on the official sites of those services.
step.ethics.indexingClaimsHint: Example: if the journal claims to be indexed in Scopus or Web of Science, verify this on scopus.com or webofscience.com. Outdated or false claims are a rejection reason.
step.ethics.misleadingMetricsExplain: DOAJ prohibits displaying metrics from commercial registries not recognised by the academic community, such as: Global Impact Factor, SJIF (Scientific Journal Impact Factor), ResearchBib IF, Universal Impact Factor, CIF, i-Factor, or similar. These are not peer-reviewed metrics and mislead authors. Only display verifiable metrics from recognised services: Web of Science Journal Impact Factor (JIF), Scopus CiteScore, SCImago SJR, or SNIP.
step.ethics.noMisleadingMetrics: The journal does NOT display non-standard or unverifiable 'impact factors' from unrecognised commercial registries.
step.bestPractice.title: 7. Best Practice
step.bestPractice.articlesHaveDois: Published articles have DOIs or other persistent identifiers.
step.bestPractice.doisHint: DOAJ recommends DOIs for all articles. DOIs ensure stable long-term links and are required by most major indexing services.
step.review.title: 8. Review & Submit
step.review.description: Review the information below, then submit to run the AI pre-assessment.
report.noIssues: No issues found. The journal appears to meet the DOAJ pre-assessment criteria checked here.
